docs.title: Mission Clocks
docs.text:
Complex tasks that require multiple actions to complete or impending threats to your unit are tracked on mission clocks. Mission cloaks are divided into segments, typically 4, 6, or 8. The more complex the task or the more time available before the threat, the more segments on the clock. Progress is tracked by marking off segments on the mission clock.

Mission clocks track complex obstacles (left) and impending threats (right).

docs.title: Track Complex Tasks
docs.text:
You'll often face complex mission objectives and obstacles, such as hacking a secure mainframe or defusing a bomb. These tasks will require multiple actions to complete. As such, the GM won't call for a single action check to determine the result. Instead, your progress toward completing the task is tracked on a mission clock.

As you complete the required sequence of actions, the GM either marks off or returns segments on the clock:

  • Failure returns 1 completed segment.
  • Partial success marks off 1 segment.
  • Complete success marks off 2 segments.
  • Critical success marks off 3 segments.

Once all segments are marked, your task is complete.

docs.title: Track Impending Threats
docs.text:
The GM uses a threat clock to track impending threats, such as a guard's alertness level or the time remaining until a high-value individual is eliminated. The threat clock is visible to all, and tension builds as it counts down.

You will certainly attempt actions to slow or eliminate the threat. However, if you fail an action check while the threat is still imminent, the GM marks off a segment on the threat clock. Once all segments are marked off, the threat occurs. The guard sounds an alarm, or the individual is eliminated.

docs.title: Character Advancement and Improving Abilities
docs.text:
You improve your character's abilities by staying true to their core drive during the mission. For example, a True Believer improves by acting ethically to further their mission.

After returning to base, describe how you met your core drive's advancement condition. If the GM agrees, choose one improvement to your character's abilities from the following table:

Improvement Effect Limit Attribute increase + 1 to one attribute Max score of 3 HP increase Roll 1D3, add to max HP No upper limit New neural weapon Roll D66, gain the result. See Neural Weapons — New specialization Choose one related to a significant action you took during a previous mission. See Specializations —

Note

If your core drive feels played out, you can choose a new one between missions, back at base, after advancing your current core drive at least once.

docs.title: Operational Preface
docs.text: During a mission, you will accumulate stress — the mental and physical wear from constant danger, sustained vigilance, and traumatic exposure. On

docs.title: Gaining Stress
docs.text:
A stress rating tracks your overall stress, starting at 0 at the start of your mission. As the mission progresses, events and circumstances will add to your rating.

Common sources of stress include:

  • Encountering anomalous entities, locations, or events
  • Failing an action roll
  • Going over 24 hours without rest, food, or water
  • Knocked unconscious
  • Riding in a vehicle hit by a heavy weapon
  • Running out of ammunition
  • Sustaining an injury
  • Taking damage
  • Thrown into darkness in hostile territory
  • Witnessing a team member or civilian die

Keep track of the stress points you accumulate as events unfold during the mission. Your character sheet has a place to record your current stress. Typically, each source adds 1 stress point. The GM will inform you when mission events or your actions increase your stress.

docs.title: Reaching Maximum Stress
docs.text:
Left unchecked, stress can degrade your performance and increase the risk of critical failures.

Your stress rating caps at 6. Whenever a stress point raises your rating to 6, your combat readiness is at risk. Make a stress check (action roll): roll 2D6 + WILLPOWER and apply the result.

Any stress points beyond 6 are ignored. However, after resolving a stress check, you may still be at 6 points. If so, no further check is required. Only the next stress point that pushes a 6 rating triggers a new check.

Roll Result 6– You panic. Roll 1D6 and consult the Panicking table below to determine the effect. 7–9 You keep it together for now. 10–12 You keep it together and remove 1 stress. 13+ You are completely locked in to the flow of combat. Remove all stress, then roll 1D6 and consult the Locked-In table below to determine the effect.

All Panicking and Locked-In effects last until the end of the mission or until you rest at a rendezvous point. See Rest and Recovery.

Example

You take damage from a gunshot (stress: 5), then watch your contact be executed (stress: 6). You make a stress check: rolls a 4 and 3, adds your WILLPOWER of +2 for a total of 9. You keep it together — for now.

docs.title: Reducing Stress
docs.text:
You can reduce your stress during a mission by following the steps below. Each option removes 1 stress point.

  • Spend your momentum, points earned from successful action rolls. See Momentum.
  • Rest at a rendezvous point, a secure location where your unit can pause and recover. See Rest and Recovery.
  • Overcome a notable opponent or major obstacle.
    • Notable opponent: A named or significant adversary whose defeat materially advances the mission: the primary target, a commanding officer, or a recurring nemesis.
    • Major obstacle: A mission-critical barrier that, if unaddressed, prevents task completion or forces an abort: a security lockdown, a timed demolition, a failed extraction point, or a severe environmental hazard.

docs.title: Panicking
docs.text:
Whenever you panic, roll 1D6 and apply the result. If you panic multiple times, the effects are cumulative.

D6 Condition Effect 1 Afraid Disadvantage on all your action rolls in combat. 2 Hopeless You fail all your initiative rolls. 3 Insulting Allies gain 1 stress whenever you see them fail an action roll. 4 Selfish Disadvantage on all your action rolls that could benefit a team member. 5 Shutdown You lose all your momentum and no longer gain any. 6 Weak You have -1 ARMOR.

docs.title: Locked-In
docs.text:
Whenever you’re locked in, roll 1D6 and apply the result. If you lock in multiple times, each effect is cumulative.

D6 Condition Effect 1 Cunning Advantage on all +TACTICS rolls. 2 Focused Advantage on all +WILLPOWER rolls. 3 Hardened You gain +1 ARMOR. 4 Jacked Advantage on all +STRENGTH rolls. 5 Sharp Advantage on all +REFLEXES rolls. 6 Steady Whenever you succeed on an action roll, team members within sight of you remove 1 stress.
